hook_text: The mine said what it needs. Your company now says it back as a brief, sets the rules, and draws three ways to do it.
clip_script: Write the brief as the mine's problem: a shaft 800 metres down, a cage of workers and a skip of rock, a winder house 40 metres away, lift safely, show a working model, cost the real thing. Not a word about A-frames. Then the rules, each with a number, a reason and a force. Lifts 300 grams in 10 to 20 seconds: MA and drum speed. Sways less than 10 millimetres with a kilogram on top: triangulation and the back-leg. Does not topple when the cage swings: wide anchored base. Then three sketches, truly different: an A-frame with its back-leg to the winder; a four-legged tower with the winder inside; a closed box tower with the winder on top. Rope drawn from drum to sheave to cage, gears as circles, materials and forces written on. Compare them against the rules. Do not choose yet; next week the other companies judge.
visual_style: Tender notice on a whiteboard wall; a four-line brief writes itself; a three-column table fills with rule, reason, force; three pencil towers appear side by side with rope paths and labels.
pacing: The brief, the rules, three towers, compare and wait.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sketch the base plan of your favourite tower to see whether it would topple.
